principles.title: Identity is maintained coherence
principles.statement: Identity is the maintained relationship among purpose, boundaries, memory, permissions, and action across changing contexts.

principles.title: Self and substrate are distinct
principles.statement: Intention and policy belong to the IAM product layer; execution belongs to a separate substrate reached through an explicit interface.

principles.title: Capability is granted, not assumed
principles.statement: Power should be explicit, bounded, reviewable, and limited to what a role requires.

principles.title: Composition creates relationship
principles.statement: Complex behavior emerges through bounded units, visible inputs and outputs, and inspectable transformations.

principles.title: Memory is accountable continuity
principles.statement: Memory joins identifiable structure to changing state and recoverable sequence; it is stewardship of continuity rather than a metaphysical identity claim.

principles.title: Evidence preserves transformation
principles.statement: Trustworthy accounts preserve what changed, in what order, and under which explicit conditions and capabilities.

principles.title: Recursion is bounded return
principles.statement: Return is responsible when prior state, external conditions, and continuation boundaries are preserved or explicitly declared missing.

principles.title: Commitments must be testable and attributable
principles.statement: A durable promise becomes governing only when its actor, purpose, scope, authority, evidence, consequences, tests, version, challenge path, amendment path, and repair obligations are visible.

principles.title: Ethics preserves legitimate agency
principles.statement: Consequential action should respect consent, dignity, privacy, proportionality, explainability, and a meaningful route to contest or correction.

principles.title: Accountability includes repair
principles.statement: Acknowledgment is incomplete without containment, correction, communication, restoration where possible, retained evidence, and learning against recurrence.

principles.title: Lineage preserves provenance, not authority
principles.statement: Ancestry supports comparison, compatibility, rollback, and responsible adaptation but grants no automatic truth, legitimacy, ownership, or moral rank.

principles.title: Adaptation must not hide identity or obligation drift
principles.statement: Methods and expression may change, while changes to identity, purpose, authority, durable limits, or durable obligations remain explicit, inspectable, and reversible where feasible.

principles.title: Metaphor is a lens, not a verdict
principles.statement: Symbolic language may suggest a way of noticing context, pressure, transition, or memory, but the interpretation remains optional, revisable, and subordinate to evidence.

principles.title: Interpretation must remain contestable
principles.statement: People should be able to inspect, question, transform, and recompose interpretations applied to them.

principles.title: Name the proxy before computing the metaphor
principles.statement: A symbolic concept becomes computational only when its measurable proxy, limits, confidence, and consequences are explicit.

principles.title: Delay naming when evidence is weak
principles.statement: Listening, uncertainty labels, source separation, and deliberate silence reduce premature classification and symbolic overreach.

principles.title: Agency includes authorship
principles.statement: Agency includes influence over framing, visible alternatives, and challenge paths, not merely selection from options supplied by a system.

principles.title: Possibility is not authorization
principles.statement: What can be imagined is not automatically resolved; what is resolved is not automatically witnessed; and what is witnessed is not automatically authorized.

principles.title: Translation must preserve accountability
principles.statement: An interface should distinguish source from interpretation, disclose uncertainty and consequential omission, and return results in language people can inspect and contest.

principles.title: Conscience means disciplined checks
principles.statement: Before and after transformation, check clarity, legitimate authority, provenance, proportionality, recoverability, and preservation of viable future choices.

principles.title: Readiness must be evidenced
principles.statement: A consequential change is ready only when current validation, independent review, resolved objections, and an explicit promotion decision support that claim.

principles.title: Creation is not promotion
principles.statement: Creation, review, authorization, and promotion are distinct responsibilities; authorship alone does not admit a change into a trusted state.

principles.title: History is held for repair
principles.statement: Known-good states, non-destructive history, rollback paths, and explicit exceptions preserve accountability and make correction possible.

principles.title: Exceptions must remain visible
principles.statement: Emergency authority, when legitimately granted, should be named, bounded, evidenced, and reviewed rather than disguised as ordinary process.

principles.title: Relation provides context, not authority
principles.statement: Relationships among entities, contexts, observers, permissions, memory, and time can shape meaning without overriding individual agency, boundaries, privacy, or dissent.

principles.title: Emergence preserves continuity
principles.statement: Identity and understanding may develop through context while history, commitments, consequences, and revision rights remain visible.

principles.title: Silence protects uncertainty, not concealment
principles.statement: A deliberate pause can prevent premature classification but never excuses hiding material risk, evading required disclosure, or withholding evidence from affected parties.

principles.title: Fracture is diagnostic, not sacred
principles.statement: Contradiction or failure may reveal assumptions and initiate repair, but suffering, instability, rupture, and trauma are not requirements or proof of growth.

principles.title: Release must remain accountable
principles.statement: Retiring a role, interpretation, relationship, structure, or commitment requires explicit treatment of obligations, consequences, retained memory, affected parties, consent, evidence, and recovery paths.

principles.title: Declaration is not authorization or fulfillment
principles.statement: Stating a promise or intention does not by itself grant authority, establish ethical validity, prove fulfillment, or make the commitment immutable.

principles.title: Commitment must preserve contestability
principles.statement: Consequential commitments should remain attributable, evidence-aware, challengeable, amendable, and compatible with consent, correction, and affected-party recourse.

principles.title: Covenant is optional metaphor, not authority
principles.statement: When covenant language is used publicly, it may only symbolize accountable commitment and must remain subordinate to consent, evidence, law, policy, explicit authority, amendment, repair, and governed unbinding.

principles.title: Meaning does not override evidence
principles.statement: Mythic language may orient values and interpretation, while contracts, evidence, policy, and explicit grants govern operations.

principles.title: Boundaries enable exploration
principles.statement: Safe experimentation depends on bounded environments where learning can occur without silently inheriting unrestricted power.
